title: 30-Minute Chicken Parm
description: Thin cutlets pan-fried and broiled with sauce and mozzarella in half an hour.
ingredients: 4 boneless chicken breasts, halved and pounded thin
steps: Pound the cutlets to 1/4 inch - thin is the whole reason this works in 30 minutes. Set up flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs mixed with half the Parmesan.
Season and coat each cutlet in flour, egg, then crumbs, pressing firmly.
Fry in the olive oil over medium-high, 2-3 minutes per side, until deep golden. Drain on a rack.
Warm the marinara in a small pan while the cutlets cook.
Put the cutlets on a sheet pan, spoon sauce over the center of each but leave the crust edges bare so they stay crisp, then top with mozzarella and the rest of the Parmesan.
Broil 2-3 minutes until the cheese bubbles and browns. Finish with torn basil.

title: Vodka Cream Pasta
description: A 20-minute pink sauce with vodka, cream and a hit of red pepper.
steps: Get the pasta water boiling before anything else - the sauce finishes in the time the pasta takes.
Cook the garlic, shallot and pepper flakes in the oil and butter over medium heat 3 minutes without browning them.
Add the vodka and let it reduce by half, about 3 minutes. The alcohol cooks off and leaves the sharpness that makes this sauce.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the cream over low heat, then tear in most of the basil.
Toss the drained pasta through the sauce with a splash of pasta water, then finish with Parmesan and the rest of the basil.

title: Buffalo Chicken Chili
description: White chili with ground chicken, hot sauce and blue cheese on top.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) cannellini beans, drained
steps: Brown the ground chicken in the oil over high heat, breaking it up, 8 minutes. Ground chicken releases a lot of water, so keep the heat high until it starts to brown rather than steam.
Add the onion, celery and garlic and cook 6 minutes.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, paprika and salt and cook 1 minute to bloom them.
Add the hot sauce and butter - together they are what makes this taste like buffalo wings rather than just spicy chili.
Add the beans and broth and simmer 15-20 minutes until thickened.
Serve topped with blue cheese and scallions, with celery sticks on the side.

title: Super Sloppy Joes
description: Sloppy joes built from scratch with brown sugar, vinegar and steak sauce.
steps: Brown the beef in the oil over high heat, breaking it up fine, 7 minutes. Drain most of the fat but leave a tablespoon.
Add the onion, bell pepper and garlic and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the brown sugar, steak sauce and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until the paste darkens.
Add the tomato sauce, vinegar, Worcestershire, chili powder, salt and pepper.
Simmer 8-10 minutes until thick enough to mound on a spoon rather than run off it.
Butter and toast the buns, then pile the filling in. Taste before serving - it wants a balance of sweet and sharp, so adjust with sugar or vinegar.

title: Weeknight Carbonara
description: Pancetta, egg and Pecorino carbonara on the table in 25 minutes.
steps: Beat the eggs, yolk, Pecorino and black pepper into a thick paste. This is the sauce - there is no cream in carbonara.
Render the pancetta in the oil over medium heat 7 minutes until crisp, then add the garlic for 1 minute and take the pan off the heat.
Boil the spaghetti to al dente and reserve 2 cups of the water.
Add the hot drained pasta to the warm pancetta pan, off the heat, and toss to coat in the fat.
Pour in the egg mixture and toss hard and fast, adding splashes of pasta water until it turns creamy. Keep the pan off the burner - any direct heat scrambles the eggs.
Serve immediately with parsley and more Pecorino. Carbonara does not wait.

title: Chicken Riggies
description: Upstate New York specialty: rigatoni with chicken, cherry peppers and cream.
steps: Season the chicken and brown it hard in the oil over high heat, 5 minutes, then set it aside. It will finish in the sauce.
Cook the onion, bell pepper and mushrooms 8 minutes until browned, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the cherry peppers and their brine. The brine is essential here - it is what gives riggies their signature sharp heat rather than just chile burn.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, then add the tomatoes and simmer 12 minutes.
Lower the heat, stir in the cream and return the chicken for 5 minutes until cooked through.
Toss with the cooked rigatoni and a splash of pasta water, then finish off the heat with the Pecorino and basil.

title: Spinach and Feta Turkey Burgers
description: Ground turkey patties packed with spinach, feta and dill.
ingredients: 10 oz frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
steps: Squeeze every drop of water out of the spinach and the grated onion. Turkey is already soft, and wet add-ins make patties that fall apart in the pan.
Mix the turkey with the spinach, feta, onion, garlic, dill, oregano, salt and pepper, handling it just enough to combine.
Form 4 patties and chill them 10 minutes if you have time - cold patties hold their shape far better.
Cook in the olive oil over medium heat 6-7 minutes per side, to 165F internal. Turkey needs lower heat and longer than beef.
Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Toast the buns and build with the yogurt sauce, lettuce, patty and tomato.

title: Chicken and Rice Stoup
description: Thicker than soup, thinner than stew - chicken, rice and vegetables in 35 minutes.
steps: Season the chicken and brown it in the oil over high heat 6 minutes, then push it to one side.
Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6 minutes, then the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice and toast it 2 minutes, then add the broth and bay leaves.
Simmer 18-20 minutes until the rice is tender. It will thicken considerably as it sits - add broth if you want it looser.
Stir in the spinach and let it wilt, 2 minutes, then discard the bay leaves.
Add the lemon juice off the heat. The acid is what keeps a rice soup from tasting heavy and flat. Serve with parsley and Parmesan.

title: Cauliflower Mac and Cheese
description: Macaroni and cauliflower in a sharp cheddar sauce, broiled on top.
ingredients: 1 head cauliflower, cut in small florets
steps: Boil the macaroni, adding the cauliflower florets for the last 5 minutes so they cook in the same pot. Drain both together.
Melt the 4 tbsp butter, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add the warm milk gradually and simmer 4 minutes until it coats a spoon.
Season with the mustard powder, nutmeg, cayenne, salt and pepper.
Take the pan off the heat before adding the cheddar and half the Parmesan, a handful at a time. Direct heat makes the sauce grainy.
Fold in the pasta and cauliflower and pour into a broiler-safe dish.
Toss the panko with the melted butter and remaining Parmesan, scatter over and broil 3-4 minutes until golden. Finish with chives.

title: Beef and Mushroom Ragu
description: A deep-tasting ragu in 40 minutes using mushrooms for body.
steps: Chop the mushrooms very fine, almost to a mince. They bring the savory depth that a long-simmered ragu would otherwise take hours to build.
Brown the beef in the oil over high heat 7 minutes, then add the mushrooms and cook 8 minutes until all their water has evaporated and they start to brown.
Add the onion, carrots and garlic and cook 6 minutes, then the tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, scraping the pan.
Add the tomatoes, thyme, salt and pepper and simmer 15 minutes, then stir in the milk - it rounds off the acidity.
Toss with the cooked rigatoni and a ladle of pasta water, then finish with Parmesan and parsley.

title: Quick Chicken Piccata
description: Lemon, caper and butter pan sauce over thin cutlets in 25 minutes.
steps: Pound the cutlets to 1/2 inch, season, and dredge in flour, shaking off the excess. That thin flour coat browns the chicken and thickens the sauce later.
Sear in the oil and 1 tbsp butter over medium-high, 3 minutes per side, then move to a plate.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the wine, and reduce by half while scraping up the browned bits.
Add the broth and lemon slices and reduce 3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the remaining butter a piece at a time. Off the heat is what emulsifies it into a sauce instead of a greasy puddle.
Add the lemon juice and capers, return the chicken briefly, and finish with parsley.

title: Quick Meatball Subs
description: Pan-fried meatballs simmered in sauce and broiled in rolls with provolone.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb ground beef and pork mix
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes. This is the difference between tender meatballs and dense ones.
Mix in the meat, egg, half the Parmesan, the garlic, parsley, salt and pepper with your hands, stopping as soon as it comes together.
Roll into 16 balls and brown them in the oil over medium-high, turning, 6 minutes. They do not need to cook through.
Add the marinara, cover, and simmer 12 minutes until the meatballs are cooked and have absorbed some sauce.
Split the rolls, toast them briefly under the broiler, then fill with meatballs and a little sauce - not so much that it soaks the bread.
Top with provolone and the rest of the Parmesan and broil 3 minutes until melted and browned. Finish with basil.

title: Steak with Gorgonzola Sauce
description: Pan-seared strip steaks under a quick gorgonzola cream sauce.
ingredients: 4 New York strip steaks (8 oz each)
steps: Pat the steaks completely dry and season them heavily. Dry surface, hot pan - that is the whole formula for a crust.
Sear in the oil over high heat 4 minutes per side for medium-rare, then move them to a board to rest.
Lower the heat, add the butter and cook the shallot 2 minutes, then the garlic for 1.
Add the wine and reduce by half, scraping up the browned bits from the steaks.
Stir in the cream and simmer 3 minutes, then add the gorgonzola off the heat and stir until just melted. Boiling blue cheese makes it bitter and grainy.
Slice the rested steaks against the grain, spoon the sauce over and finish with chives and thyme.

title: Quick Italian Wedding Soup
description: Tiny meatballs and pasta in broth with escarole, in 40 minutes.
ingredients: 1 lb ground beef and pork mix
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk 5 minutes, then mix with the meat, egg, half the Parmesan, garlic, parsley, 1 tsp salt and the pepper.
Roll into very small meatballs, about 3/4 inch. Marble-sized is traditional and they cook through in the broth in minutes.
Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the oil 8 minutes, then add the broth and bring to a gentle simmer.
Drop the meatballs in and simmer 10 minutes. Do not stir hard for the first few minutes or they break apart.
Add the pasta and cook 8 minutes, then the escarole for 2-3 minutes until wilted.
Season with the remaining salt, the nutmeg and the lemon juice, and serve with the rest of the Parmesan.

title: Sausage and Peppers Skillet
description: Italian sausage, peppers and onions in one pan with vinegar at the end.
steps: Brown the whole sausages in the oil over medium-high, turning, 8 minutes. Do not prick them - the casings hold the juices in.
Move the sausages out and add the peppers and onions to the pan. Cook over high heat 8 minutes until charred at the edges.
Add the garlic, pepper flakes, oregano, salt and pepper for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine, return the sausages, and simmer 8 minutes until the sausages reach 160F and the wine has mostly cooked away.
Add the vinegar off the heat and toss. The splash of acid at the end is what lifts the whole pan out of richness.
Slice the sausages, add the parsley, and pile into rolls or serve over polenta.

title: Philly Cheesesteak Sloppy Joes
description: Ground beef with peppers and onions in a provolone cheese sauce, on rolls.
steps: Brown the beef in the oil over high heat 7 minutes, then drain most of the fat.
Add the onion, bell pepper and mushrooms and cook 8 minutes until the mushrooms have browned and lost their water.
Add the garlic, Worcestershire, broth, salt and pepper and simmer 6 minutes until thick enough to hold on a spoon.
In a separate pan, melt the butter, whisk in the flour for 2 minutes, then add the milk gradually and simmer 3 minutes until thick.
Take the cheese sauce off the heat before stirring in the provolone - it strings and goes oily if it boils.
Pile the beef mixture into split rolls and pour the cheese sauce over. Finish with parsley.

title: Grilled Pizza
description: Pizza dough cooked straight on the grill grate for a smoky, blistered base.
steps: Let the dough come to room temperature, then divide into 4 and stretch each by hand into a rough oval 1/4 inch thick.
Brush both sides generously with olive oil and season. Oil is what keeps the dough from welding to the grate.
Heat the grill to medium-high and scrape the grates clean. Lay the dough directly on the grate and cook 2-3 minutes until it puffs and the underside is marked.
Flip, then work fast: spread sauce thinly, add the mozzarella, Parmesan, tomatoes and pepperoni.
Close the lid for 3-4 minutes, until the cheese melts and the bottom is crisp. Longer than that and the base burns, so have your toppings ready before the dough goes on.
Slide onto a board, add the pepper flakes, oregano and torn basil, and cut into strips.

title: Caesar Pasta Salad
description: Pasta salad dressed like a Caesar, with romaine and garlic croutons.
ingredients: 1/4 cup olive oil, for the croutons
steps: Toss the bread cubes with the 1/4 cup oil and a pinch of salt and bake at 400F for 12 minutes until golden and dry through. Cool completely.
Cook the pasta just past al dente - it firms up as it chills - then rinse under cold water and drain well.
Mash the anchovies and garlic to a paste with the flat of a knife. They give the dressing its savory backbone and will not taste fishy.
Whisk in the egg yolks, lemon juice, Dijon and Worcestershire, then add the 2/3 cup oil in a very thin stream, whisking constantly so it emulsifies.
Stir in half the Parmesan and season. Toss with the pasta and chill 1 hour.
Just before serving, fold in the romaine, tomatoes, croutons, parsley and remaining Parmesan. Add the croutons last so they stay crisp.

title: Tuscan Chicken and White Bean Skillet
description: Chicken thighs with cannellini beans, kale and rosemary in one skillet.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) cannellini beans, drained
steps: Season the chicken and brown it in the oil over high heat 5 minutes per side, then set aside.
Cook the onion in the same pan 5 minutes, then the garlic, pepper flakes and rosemary for 1 minute.
Add the wine and reduce by half, scraping up the browned bits.
Mash about a third of the beans, then add all of them with the broth. The mashed beans thicken the pan into a sauce without any cream.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer 10 minutes until cooked through.
Stir in the kale and cook 4 minutes until tender, then add the lemon juice off the heat and serve with Parmesan.

title: Shrimp Fra Diavolo
description: Shrimp in a fiery garlic-chile tomato sauce over linguine in 30 minutes.
steps: Get the pasta water boiling first - the sauce takes exactly as long as the linguine.
Pat the shrimp dry and sear them in 2 tbsp of the oil over high heat, 1 minute per side, then pull them out. They finish in the sauce, and overcooking here is the one way to ruin this.
Add the rest of the oil, the garlic, pepper flakes and cayenne and cook 1 minute. Fra diavolo means brother devil, so do not be timid with the chile.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, then add the tomatoes, salt and oregano and simmer 12 minutes.
Toss in the drained linguine with a splash of pasta water.
Return the shrimp for 1-2 minutes only, swirl in the butter off the heat, then add the parsley and lemon juice. No cheese with this one.

title: Pork Chops with Apples and Onions
description: Seared chops with cider-glazed apples and onions in the same pan.
steps: Pat the chops very dry and season well. Sear them in the oil over high heat 4 minutes per side until deeply browned, then move to a plate - they are not cooked through yet.
Lower the heat, add the butter and cook the onions 6 minutes until soft.
Add the apples, thyme and brown sugar and cook 5 minutes until the apples start to caramelize at the edges.
Pour in the cider and vinegar and let it bubble down by half, scraping the pan.
Whisk in the Dijon, then return the chops with their juices and simmer 6-8 minutes, turning once, to 145F internal.
Rest the chops 5 minutes before serving with the apples and pan sauce and a scatter of parsley.

title: French Onion Burgers
description: Burgers topped with caramelized onions and melted Gruyere on toasted rolls.
steps: Cook the onions in the butter and 1 tbsp oil over medium-low for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until deeply browned and jammy. There is no way to rush this - high heat gives you burnt edges and raw middles.
Add the thyme, wine and Worcestershire and let it reduce until almost dry, 5 minutes.
Stir the mayonnaise with the Dijon.
Form 4 loose patties wider than the rolls, dimple the centers, and season just before cooking.
Cook in the remaining oil over high heat 3-4 minutes per side for medium.
Pile the onions on each patty, cover with Gruyere and put a lid on the pan for 1 minute to melt. Toast the rolls, spread with the Dijon mayo and build.

title: Baked Ziti with Spinach
description: Ziti with ricotta, spinach and sausage, baked in 45 minutes start to finish.
ingredients: 10 oz frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
steps: Boil the ziti 3 minutes short of al dente. It finishes in the oven, and fully cooked pasta turns to mush in a bake.
Brown the sausage in the oil, then add the onion for 5 minutes, the garlic and pepper flakes for 1, then the tomatoes and salt. Simmer 12 minutes.
Squeeze the spinach completely dry - wet spinach makes a watery bake - then mix it with the ricotta, egg and half the Parmesan.
Toss the drained pasta with most of the sauce.
Layer half the pasta in a 9x13 dish, dollop the ricotta mixture over, add the rest of the pasta, remaining sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake at 425F for 20-25 minutes until bubbling and browned. Rest 10 minutes and finish with basil.

title: 30-Minute Chicken and Dumplings
description: Creamy chicken stew with drop biscuit dumplings steamed on top.
steps: Season the chicken and brown it in the oil and 2 tbsp butter over high heat 6 minutes, then add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, then the flour, and stir 2 minutes. Whisk in the broth gradually so it stays smooth, then the cream and thyme.
Simmer 8 minutes until thickened, then stir in the peas.

Rub the cold butter into the self-rising flour with your fingertips until pea-sized, then stir in the cold buttermilk to a shaggy dough. Mix as little as possible - overworked dumplings come out heavy.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the surface of the simmering stew, leaving gaps.
Cover tightly and steam 12-15 minutes without lifting the lid. The trapped steam is what cooks them through, so peeking costs you the rise. Finish with parsley.

title: Ricotta and Honey Toasts
description: Whipped ricotta on grilled bread with honey, lemon and pistachios.
ingredients: 3 tbsp olive oil, for the bread
steps: Whip the ricotta with the 2 tbsp olive oil, lemon zest and salt for 2 minutes until it goes from grainy to genuinely smooth and light. That whipping is the only technique in the dish and it makes all the difference.
Brush the bread with the remaining oil and grill or broil until charred at the edges but still chewy in the middle.
Spread the whipped ricotta thickly on the warm toasts.
Drizzle generously with honey.
Scatter the pistachios, flaky salt and a little black pepper over. The salt and pepper against the honey are what keep this from being merely sweet.
Serve immediately, while the bread is still warm.
